newsitem.title: INDIA: India hikes jet fuel prices for foreign carriers.
newsitem.headline: India hikes jet fuel prices for foreign carriers.

text.p: India's state-run oil refiners raised jet fuel prices by one cent a gallon with immediate effect, an official of one of the firms said on Wednesday.

An official of Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd said the new price would be 99 cents per gallon or $261.53 for 1,000 litres. He said the price revision applied only to foreign airlines, and not to domestic carriers.
"We have a separate billing system for them," the official said about foreign airlines which are billed in dollars. "They are not charged local taxes. There is also a subsidy element."
Prices of most petroleum products are fixed by the government. Prices of several products are inflated to pay for subsidised prices of kerosene and liquified petroleum gas.
The official did not give reasons for the price hike in jet fuel but oil analysts said this was part of the government's effort to plug the rising oil subsidy bill.
